comparison: Perfect agreement on C22 and C23 regarding associative learning task performance. Both evaluations find the behavioral data strongly supports that participants formed face-scene associations. OpenEval emphasizes this as a prerequisite for main hypotheses; peer reviewers praised the 'well-controlled experiment' with 'solid and convincing' results.

Strong agreement on C5-C7 and C28-C32 regarding face decoding during cue period. Both evaluations support these findings as expected given visual presentation. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical tests; peer reviewers stated 'results are solid and convincing' and 'statistical analyses are all sound.'

Complete agreement on C9 and C33-C36 regarding vLPFC decoding during cue period as evidence of memory retrieval. Both evaluations accept the interpretation that vLPFC reflects memory retrieval. OpenEval notes some p-values are uncorrected; peer reviewers acknowledged 'the face and the scene have been associated and that this can be seen in the fMRI data.'

Full agreement on C8, C37, and C43 regarding absence of face decoding during delay period. Both evaluations support this null result as critical for the main interpretation that scene information supplants face information. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Strong agreement on C10-C11 and C38-C42, C66 regarding scene decoding during delay period. Both evaluations view this as the key finding providing compelling evidence for memory-evoked scene representations. OpenEval notes one uncorrected p-value; peer reviewers called it 'compelling' and 'strongly supports invoking of a very specific attentional template.'

Divergence on main conclusion (C12, C74, C75). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on double dissociation pattern, acknowledging correlational limitations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 questioning whether findings are specific to search versus general associative recall, noting 'the linkage between these two results is not entirely clear.'

Perfect agreement on C46 and C47 regarding behavioral scene validity effects. Both evaluations accept these results as straightforward evidence that participants used scene information to guide search. OpenEval notes consistency with neural findings; peer reviewers stated 'it is also clear that a valid scene background speeds the behavioral response.'

Complete agreement on C48-C53 regarding univariate activation patterns and cognitive control interpretation. Both evaluations support the prediction error and template switching interpretation. OpenEval notes causal limitations of fMRI; peer reviewers stated 'statistical analyses are all sound and the results integrate well with previous findings.'

Agreement on C44 regarding whole-brain searchlight null results. Both evaluations accept this finding as strengthening the interpretation of distinct networks. OpenEval cautions about interpreting null results; peer reviewers accepted without challenge after authors conducted requested delay period split analysis.

Agreement on C45 regarding temporal analysis of delay period. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to exploratory nature and potential power issues. Peer reviewers initially requested this analysis, then accepted the null result stating 'I have no further comments or concerns' after authors provided explanation.

Full agreement on C54 and C55 regarding IFJ subregion heterogeneity. Both evaluations accept this as a supported secondary observation about functional and anatomical differences within IFJ. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Complete agreement on C67 and C68 regarding FEF null results and speculative explanation. Both evaluations accept the null finding and the explanation about lack of spatial cues. OpenEval cautions about interpreting null results; peer reviewers accepted without objection.

Full agreement on C73 regarding fMRI correlational limitations. Both evaluations accept this as an appropriate acknowledgment of methodological constraints. OpenEval explicitly praises the acknowledgment; peer reviewers implicitly accepted this standard limitation.

Complete agreement on C70-C72 regarding boundary conditions and context-dependence of findings. Both evaluations accept these as reasonable interpretations about when scene information would be prioritized. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

OpenEval evaluated C77-C81 regarding sample size justification and participant exclusions as SUPPORTED, finding the power analysis appropriate and exclusion criteria reasonable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these methodological details.

OpenEval evaluated C61 and C62 as SUPPORTED, emphasizing the logical inference that scene decoding during delay must reflect memory retrieval rather than stimulus-driven responses. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addressed this interpretive point.
